_comment: WHAT THE GAME TEACHES ABOUT ITSELF, and when.

Kent, playing Level 1: 'its just knowledge dumping at this point, i feel so overwhelmed, why are the instructions popping everywhere ... when there is instructions it is better that the screen goes dim and then that part is highlighted'. And before that: 'not like those just text but add visuals like the button itself ... there are players that will play it without reading it'.

So a lesson is a CARD in one of two places (top or bottom centre, away from what it is about), over a dimmed screen with a hole lit where the lesson is, and the card is first a PICTURE -- `visual` -- of the key or mouse doing the thing, then a short `caption`. TutorialSpotlight draws it; TutorialDirector decides when. One at a time, a breath between them, nothing over anyone talking.

`mode`: `do` lessons keep the world running and go the moment the player presses what they show (the press still does its job); `look` lessons stop the world -- they are about a reading that moves, the clock, the ink -- and any key or click dismisses them. `say` is Lolo remarking rather than the game instructing, and goes to his hint bar over the apo.
`delay` is how long a lesson waits, once its moment has come, before it shows. If the player does the thing in that time it is spent unshown: a player who walks at once is never told how to walk.

`context` (world / placing / creature / canvas / any) is when it may show; `anchor` is what it lights up, resolved by LevelBase._tutorial_target -- the tutorial's own vocabulary, not node paths. A lesson whose context or anchor does not hold waits for it, and gives up after `patience` seconds (default 8) to be offered again by its event.

KEYS ARE NOT WRITTEN HERE. `action` (plus `through` for a pair or a numbered run) is read off the live InputMap and drawn as caps, so a rebinding cannot leave a lesson showing a key that no longer does anything. `mouse` lists the mouse inputs a lesson teaches: left, right, wheel, shift_wheel. `text` is the full sentence, still what the hint bar says when there is no spotlight, and what the audits read.

NO LESSON MAY NAME A DRAWABLE CLASS, in its text or its caption. Same rule as the dialogue: `key`, `door`, `wheel` are all classes and all answers somewhere. The pictures follow it too: 'your drawing' is drawn as a scrap of paper with a scribble on it, never a shape.

`at` is the event that offers a lesson; `after` holds it back until another has been spent, so the order survives a player who does things out of sequence. Cut on this pass because they were the dumping: `pause` (Escape is the one key everybody already knows), `sure` (the confidence number is shown on the card; explaining it at the second second of a ten-second life was a third card in a row), `sign` (the E READ prompt already says it), and the canvas briefing, four lines of Lolo inside the panel -- the canvas is now taught by two cards that only appear if the player hesitates.
